svg.title: Sell the Outcome Before Building the System
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-outcome-first-offer; chapter number: 1; title: Sell the Outcome Before Building the System; subtitle: Find a paying business problem, bound the package, customize delivery, and prove the result.; caption: Nate Herk emphasizes time, money, and focus; Noah Epstein collects payment before building; Mikey No Code defines the package and demonstrates its business result.; assumptions note: Nate Herk, Noah Epstein, and Mikey No Code describe complementary approaches, not a jointly reported engagement. Mikey's commercial terms are an example offer, not receipts.; note: Nate Herk — SAerRtQLD0I at 00:01:33 and 00:04:08; Noah Epstein — fMdUS6amki0 at 00:02:14; Mikey No Code — i4z0kCcByY8 at 00:29:31, 00:29:51, 00:33:46, and 00:38:08.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Choose the business result; value: Step 1; detail: Nate Herk frames the offer around time, money, and focus rather than workflow nodes or models.; step: 02; label: Secure paid demand; value: Step 2; detail: Noah Epstein identifies a business willing to pay and collects payment before committing to the build.; step: 03; label: Bound the initial package; value: Step 3; detail: Mikey No Code specifies connected tools, an initial three-agent limit, and setup-payment terms. Their example is $2,500 setup plus $750 monthly.; step: 04; label: Customize the reusable base; value: Step 4; detail: Nate Herk uses the business owner's subject-matter expertise to customize the system; a template bundle alone is not the service.; step: 05; label: Demonstrate the result; value: Step 5; detail: Mikey No Code recommends a two- or three-minute Loom showing the arriving lead, response, routing decision, and final report.
